extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models. It comprises 1,500 challenging samples meticulously selected by humans, covering 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, with samples curated to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capability requirements.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen; Jinsong Li; Xiaoyi Dong; Pan Zhang; Yuhang Zang; Zehui Chen; Haodong Duan; Jiaqi Wang; Yu Qiao; Dahua Lin; Feng Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, and Feng Zhao. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv preprint arXiv:2403.20330v2, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline, then manually reviewed by three experts to curate 1,500 high-quality samples for MMStar.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples were collected from six existing benchmarks: MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline, then three experts manually review the coarsely filtered samples to ensure each sample’s answer is based on understanding visual content, covers capability assessment dimensions, and requires advanced multi-modal abilities; after considering diversity and difficulty levels, they manually curated 1,500 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: They document hit frequency for each sample using LLM inspectors and retain only samples with hit counts of two or fewer; for manual selection, they tally hit counts of 16 LVLMs on coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo; GeminiPro; Qwen-1.5-72B; InternLM2-20B; Yi-34B; Deepseek-67B; Mixtral-8x7B; LLaMA2-70B; GPT4V; GeminiPro-Vision; LLaVA series
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Even the best model scores under 60 on average on MMStar; no LVLMs managed to reach a passing average score (i.e. 60%) in the core capabilities of fine-grained perception, logical reasoning, science & technology, and mathematics, highlighting these dimensions as particularly challenging for existing LVLMs.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The existence of inappropriate questions and data leaking would lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLM; for research to be transparent and equitable, it is imperative to account for and mitigate such leakage so models are evaluated on their true ability to integrate and interpret multi-modal data, rather than their capacity to memorize specific samples.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities; assess their multi-modal capabilities; investigate data leakage and actual multi-modal gain; provide a comprehensive and fair arena for comparing existing LVLMs
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline... Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs are excluded as they may exist leaking or visual-unnecessary problems... Finally, we only retain those samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits... To expedite the manual selection of samples with varying difficulty levels for LVLMs, we tally the hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Finally, after considering both the diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels, we manually curated 1,500 high-quality samples from the coarsely filtered set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Given that all questions are ensured to be converted into a multiple-choice format, we develop some heuristic matching rules to calculate accuracy, avoiding the cumbersome process of re-invoking GPT4 for answer extraction.
